design_notes.D-F0: ROUND-7 CORRECTION 1 of 2 (FLAG-CORE-OBJECT-MISFIT on def:cty-distance-risk / thm:cty-same-class-log-converse): R_n^NP RETURNS TO THE CORE'S COMPLETED EXPECTATION, and the missing bridge is sized and routed instead of designed around. THE FLAG, accepted in full: round 5 encoded R_n^NP's expectation as Mathlib's `MeasureTheory.lintegral` on the BASE Borel sigma-algebra. That is the LOWER integral, which for a non-measurable integrand is in general STRICTLY SMALLER than the completed expectation the core displays; proving a lower bound on it is a weaker obligation dressed as a stronger-looking one, and — this is the substance of the flag — it silently REPLACES the declared risk functional rather than realising it. A plan may strengthen a bound; it may not redefine the object the bound is about. THE REPAIR, at the definition so that no consumer can drift from it: the inner expectation of R_n^NP is now `∫⁻ w, (boundary-supremum loss) ∂((P.law.pi n).completion)`, taken against `MeasureTheory.Measure.completion` (Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Measure/NullMeasurable.lean:444, `Measure alpha -> Measure (NullMeasurableSpace alpha mu)`), i.e. the measure read on the COMPLETED sigma-algebra. This IS the core's E_P: whenever the integrand is measurable for the completion — which, for a member of the CTY common-map class, is exactly what the core's own proof establishes via analytic projection — the two agree by definition of the Lebesgue integral of a completion-measurable function, and the value is the completed expectation of the (then existing) measurable version. The ℝ≥0∞ ambient of D-D0 is retained, so the three quantifiers stay total in a complete lattice; only the MEASURE the expectation is taken against moves, from the base sigma-algebra to its completion. THE BRIDGE, SIZED AND ROUTED rather than bypassed (the reviewer's explicit instruction): the fact the core's route needs is that the projection of a Borel set is analytic and analytic sets are UNIVERSALLY MEASURABLE (Choquet capacitability). Mathlib has the AnalyticSet layer but NOT that theorem (search trace re-run this round, survey ROUND-7 (B)); it is a LARGE upstream, Mathlib-grade contribution and it is externally established classical descriptive set theory, not this paper's content. It is therefore listed EXPLICITLY as infrastructure item I-1 (kind mathlib-lemma, effort large) with its exact statement and its exact consumers, and F2/F3 scaffold the two named non-node helpers it would discharge — `boundary_sup_completion_measurable` (for a CtyRule, the boundary loss supremum is completion-measurable) and `ctyRisk_eq_completed_expectation` (hence R_n^NP is literally the core's inf-sup of completed expectations, and R_n^NP >= R_n^PI as the core's proof_tex displays) — as `sorry`-free-optional statements consumed by NOTHING in the theorem manifest. IT IS NON-BLOCKING, and here is the honest accounting of why, which F1.5 should check rather than take on trust: t3 proves a LOWER bound, and the completed integral DOMINATES the base lower integral (every base-measurable simple minorant is completion-measurable with the same integral), so the auxiliary base-lower-integral bound of round 5 now enters only as an intermediate step INSIDE a proof about the completed expectation, which is precisely the reviewer's 'lower integration may remain an auxiliary bound'. Concretely t3 goes: L_fin is Borel-measurable, so `∫⁻ L_fin ∂mu = ∫⁻ L_fin ∂mu.completion` (helper `lintegral_completion_of_measurable`, via `MeasureTheory.lintegral_trim`); L_fin <= boundary sup pointwise, so `MeasureTheory.lintegral_mono` IN THE COMPLETION gives `∫⁻ boundary-sup ∂mu.completion >= c a_n`. No universal measurability is used, and NOTHING is assumed: the delivered t3 is a lower bound on the completed expectation itself. Without I-1 the plan cannot additionally prove that the completed expectation is an honest expectation of a random variable (that is I-1's content and the core's own presupposition); with I-1 it can, and the statement t3 delivers does not change either way. That is the difference from round 5, where the bypass silently shrank the object. DEPENDENCY CLOSURE, derived by tracing the core's depends_on rather than read off the flag: R_n^NP is bound by S3 and constructed by def:cty-distance-risk, whose ONLY consumer is thm:cty-same-class-log-converse (t3); so the edited set is S3 (modules and notes), def:cty-distance-risk (encoding), t3 (route, modules, the I-1 routing), Helpers/OuterExpectation.lean and Basic.lean in file_layout, and assumption_classification.no_silent_gates. Scaffold shape F2 must follow: `lemma cty_winsorization_bias (P : A1A2Law) (hP : A1A2Class p nu L P) {B : R} (hB : 1 <= B) (t : Bool) {x : Score} (hx : x ∈ P.support) : |(∫ y, y ∂(P.condKer t x)) - (∫ y, winsorize B y ∂(P.condKer t x))| <= L * B ^ (-3 : Z)|` -- a genuinely pointwise inequality about a genuinely pointwise object, with NO a.e. caveat anywhere in the statement. THE PROOF IS THEN THE THREE-LINE COMPUTATION the core displays, entirely inside the fixed measure `P.condKer t x`: combine the two integrals by `integral_sub` (both integrable, the winsorized one by boundedness and the raw one from the clause-(v) envelope at this same x via `MeasureTheory.MemLp.integrable`); bound the integrand pointwise by `|y - winsorize B y| = (|y| - B)_+ <= |y| * 1{|y| > B} <= |y|^(2+nu) / B^(1+nu) <= |y|^(2+nu) / B^3` using nu >= 2 and B >= 1; then `integral_mono` / `norm_integral_le_integral_norm` and clause (v) of def:cty-a1-a2-class, which is now literally `∫ |y|^(2+nu) ∂(P.condKer t x) <= L`. If a proof step genuinely needs `condDistrib` rather than the selected version, `ProbabilityTheory.condDistrib_ae_eq_of_measure_eq_compProd_of_measurable` supplies the a.e. identification, and that is the ONLY place an a.e. statement appears on this chain. citations.statement: Uniform first-order approximation-bias guarantee for the signed-distance local-polynomial contrast along deterministic bandwidth sequences with h decreasing to zero and n h^2 tending to infinity.
citations.verbatim_statement: Theorem 2 (Approximation Bias: Uniform Guarantee). For some L ≥ 1, let P be the class satisfying Assumption 1(i)–(iii), X ⊆ [−L,L]², Assumption 2, L⁻¹ ≤ inf_X f_X ≤ sup_X f_X ≤ L, the displayed uniform order-p derivative/Lipschitz bound on μ_t, and liminf_{h↓0} inf_{x∈B} ∫_{A_t} K_h((2t−1)d(u,x))du ≥ L⁻¹ for each t. For any p ≥ 0, if nh² → ∞ and h → 0, then 1 ≲ liminf_n sup_{P∈P} sup_{x∈B}|B(x)|/h ≤ limsup_n sup_{P∈P} sup_{x∈B}|B(x)|/h ≲ 1.

citations.statement: Expected maximal-inequality displays for the degree-p signed-distance Gram and centred-score processes with the uniform kernel.
citations.verbatim_statement: In SA-8.3, after establishing VC-type entropy for the Gram-entry class G (including the uniform-kernel case via Assumption SA-2(iii)), the maximal inequality yields E[sup_{l∈G}|E_n l(X_i)−E l(X_i)|] ≲ sqrt(log(1/h)/(n h^d)); finite dimensionality gives the corresponding uniform Gram-process bound. In SA-8.4, for the centered score class F, the maximal inequality yields E[sup_{x∈B}|e_ℓᵀ O_{t,x}|] ≲ sqrt(log(1/h)/(n h^d)) + log(1/h)/(n^((1+ν)/(2+ν)) h^d); finite dimensionality and Lemma SA-3 give the vector and stabilized consequences.

attestation.note: Main inspected the authors’ open-access May 25, 2026 supplement at the recorded URL on 2026-08-10; transcribed the expected maximal-inequality conclusions and their stated finite-dimensional consequences from SA-8.3 printed pp. 32–33 and SA-8.4 printed pp. 33–35 (PDF pages 34–37, text lines 3245–3688).

file_layout.Causal/EmpiricalProcess/Separability.lea: ROUND-13 NEW (D-M0), the irreducible residual and the ONLY genuinely new mathematics in the replacement chain. The countable-index bridge for the winsorized score class: a fixed countable subfamily G_0 of the continuum-indexed class G whose POINTWISE supremum of |(P_n - P) g| equals that of G, so that `MeasureTheory.outerLIntegral` of the class supremum collapses to an ordinary `lintegral` of a measurable countable supremum and every `[Countable iota]` engine in Causalean applies verbatim. THREE PIECES. (1) The b-direction is continuous, so `separableSpaceSup_eq_real` (FoML, re-exported at Causalean/Stat/Concentration/Covering/Separable.lean) applies off the shelf on the closed ball ‖b‖ <= C_0. (2) The x-direction is discontinuous ONLY through the closed kernel indicator `1{‖z - x‖_2 <= h}`; the index is enlarged by a rational bandwidth window h' in [h, 2h] and rational centres, and pointwise convergence is proved in three cases (strictly inside, strictly outside, and the boundary case ‖z - x‖ = h, covered because ‖z - x_m‖ <= ‖z - x‖ + ‖x - x_m‖ < h' eventually). The enlargement is FREE in entropy: lem:euclidean-balls-vc (t6) bounds the VC index of closed Euclidean balls of ALL radii by four, which is exactly core clause (vii), and the variance bound sigma <~ h survives at radius 2h. (3) Transfer of pointwise convergence to `(P_n - P) g`: a finite sum on the empirical side, dominated convergence with the constant envelope C(p,L) B on the population side. Projected ~320 lines. Imports Causal/{Estimator,EuclideanBallsVC,LawClass}.lean and the Causalean Covering layer.

THIS FILE CARRIES THE PLAN'S RESIDUAL RISK and is the honest escalation locus if F3 stalls: the crude Dudley bound at envelope U = C(p,L) B does NOT suffice (the leading term must scale with sigma ~ h, not with B), so step (iii) is where the work concentrates.
